description: Comprehensive question bank for FDA/SDA Computer Knowledge - Email (18.7). Covers all topics from the provided study material: Email fundamentals, To/CC/BCC, composing and managing messages, SMTP/POP3/IMAP, attachments, professional etiquette, spam, phishing, privacy and security. Questions are structured for KEA examination preparation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email?

options.A: A method of sending and receiving digital messages over computer networks, especially the Internet
options.B: A social media platform for sharing photos
options.C: A type of computer hardware used for storage
options.D: A programming language used for web development

questions.explanation: Email (electronic mail) is a method of sending and receiving digital messages over computer networks, especially the Internet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the term 'email' stand for?

options.A: Electronic mail
options.B: Emergency mail
options.C: Express mail
options.D: External mail

questions.explanation: Email stands for electronic mail.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main purpose of email?

options.A: To exchange messages and digital information electronically between individuals or groups
options.B: To store files permanently on a computer
options.C: To edit images and videos
options.D: To install software applications

questions.explanation: The main purpose of email is to exchange messages and digital information electronically between individuals or groups.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email address?

options.A: A unique address used to identify an email mailbox or recipient
options.B: A physical location of a computer
options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A software application for editing documents

questions.explanation: An email address is a unique address used to identify an email mailbox or recipient, usually written in the form local-part@domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the basic parts of a typical email address?

options.A: The local part, the @ symbol and the domain part
options.B: The username, password and PIN
options.C: The header, body and footer
options.D: The sender, recipient and subject

questions.explanation: The basic parts of a typical email address are the local part, the @ symbol and the domain part; for example, student@example.com.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the @ symbol separate in an email address?

options.A: It separates the local part from the domain name
options.B: It separates the subject from the body
options.C: It separates the sender from the recipient
options.D: It separates the attachment from the message

questions.explanation: The @ symbol separates the local part (mailbox or account name) from the domain name.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the local part of an email address?

options.A: The part before the @ symbol that identifies the mailbox or recipient within a domain
options.B: The part after the @ symbol that identifies the mail domain
options.C: The part that contains the email subject
options.D: The part that stores the email attachments

questions.explanation: The local part is the part before the @ symbol that identifies the mailbox or recipient within a domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the domain part of an email address?

options.A: The part after the @ symbol that identifies the mail domain responsible for receiving the email
options.B: The part before the @ symbol that identifies the mailbox
options.C: The part that contains the email password
options.D: The part that stores sent messages

questions.explanation: The domain part is the part after the @ symbol that identifies the mail domain responsible for receiving the email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email mailbox?

options.A: A storage area associated with an email account where messages are received and maintained
options.B: A physical box used for postal mail
options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A software for editing spreadsheets

questions.explanation: An email mailbox is a storage area associated with an email account where messages are received and maintained.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email client?

options.A: A software application used to compose, send, receive, organise and manage email messages
options.B: A person who receives emails
options.C: A server that stores emails
options.D: A type of email address

questions.explanation: An email client is a software application used to compose, send, receive, organise and manage email messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an email service?

options.A: Gmail
options.B: Microsoft Word
options.C: Adobe Photoshop
options.D: VLC Media Player

questions.explanation: Gmail, Outlook.com, Yahoo Mail and Proton Mail are examples of email services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a desktop email client?

options.A: Microsoft Outlook
options.B: Google Chrome
options.C: Windows Explorer
options.D: Notepad

questions.explanation: Microsoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird and Apple Mail are examples of desktop email clients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is webmail?

options.A: An email service accessed through a web browser
options.B: An email service that only works offline
options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A protocol used for sending emails

questions.explanation: Webmail is an email service accessed through a web browser rather than only through a dedicated desktop email application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between webmail and an email client?

options.A: Webmail is accessed through a browser; an email client is an application that manages email and may connect to one or more mail services
options.B: Webmail is faster than email client
options.C: Email client is only for sending, webmail is only for receiving
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: Webmail is accessed through a browser; an email client is an application that manages email and may connect to one or more mail services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Who is widely credited with implementing network email on ARPANET?

options.A: Ray Tomlinson
options.B: Bill Gates
options.C: Steve Jobs
options.D: Tim Berners-Lee

questions.explanation: Ray Tomlinson is widely credited with implementing network email on ARPANET in 1971 and popularising the use of @ between the user name and host.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: In which year did Ray Tomlinson implement network email on ARPANET?
questions.explanation: Network email is commonly dated to have been developed by Ray Tomlinson in 1971.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email message?

options.A: A digital communication consisting of message headers and a message body, with optional attachments
options.B: A physical letter sent through postal service
options.C: A type of computer virus
options.D: A software application for video editing

questions.explanation: An email message is a digital communication consisting of message headers and a message body, with optional attachments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are email headers?

options.A: Message fields containing information such as sender, recipient, subject, date, routing details and other metadata
options.B: The main content of the email
options.C: The attachments included in the email
options.D: The password used to access the email account

questions.explanation: Email headers are message fields containing information such as sender, recipient, subject, date, routing details and other metadata.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the subject line of an email?

options.A: A short heading that summarises the purpose or topic of the message
options.B: The main content of the email
options.C: The sender's email address
options.D: The attachment file name

questions.explanation: The subject line of an email is a short heading that summarises the purpose or topic of the message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the body of an email?

options.A: The main content or message text written by the sender
options.B: The subject line of the email
options.C: The email address of the recipient
options.D: The server that stores the email

questions.explanation: The body of an email is the main content or message text written by the sender.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email signature?

options.A: A block of text automatically or manually added to the end of an email, often containing the sender's name, role and contact details
options.B: A digital signature used to encrypt emails
options.C: The password of the email account
options.D: The subject line of the email

questions.explanation: An email signature is a block of text automatically or manually added to the end of an email, often containing the sender's name, role and contact details.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email thread or conversation?

options.A: A group of related messages, usually linked by replies to an earlier email
options.B: A single email message
options.C: The subject line of an email
options.D: The attachment of an email

questions.explanation: An email thread or conversation is a group of related messages, usually linked by replies to an earlier email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email alias?

options.A: An alternative email address that forwards to or is associated with another mailbox
options.B: A fake email address used for spam
options.C: The password of an email account
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: An email alias is an alternative email address that forwards to or is associated with another mailbox, depending on the service.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email distribution list?

options.A: A named list of recipients used to send one message to multiple people
options.B: A list of all emails in the inbox
options.C: A list of email attachments
options.D: A list of email passwords

questions.explanation: An email distribution list is a named list of recipients used to send one message to multiple people.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email group?

options.A: A group address or service that distributes messages to multiple members
options.B: A folder that stores sent emails
options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A software for editing documents

questions.explanation: An email group is a group address or service that distributes messages to multiple members.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email server?

options.A: A server that sends, receives, routes or stores email messages
options.B: A computer used only for gaming
options.C: A type of email address
options.D: A software for creating presentations

questions.explanation: An email server is a server that sends, receives, routes or stores email messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Mail User Agent (MUA)?

options.A: An email application or client used by a person to compose, read and manage messages
options.B: Software that transfers email between mail servers
options.C: Software that delivers incoming mail to a mailbox
options.D: A server that stores email messages

questions.explanation: A Mail User Agent (MUA) is an email application or client used by a person to compose, read and manage messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Mail Transfer Agent (MTA)?

options.A: Software that transfers email between mail servers using mail-transfer protocols such as SMTP
options.B: An email application used by a person to read messages
options.C: Software that delivers incoming mail to a recipient's mailbox
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: A Mail Transfer Agent (MTA) is software that transfers email between mail servers using mail-transfer protocols such as SMTP.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Mail Delivery Agent (MDA)?

options.A: Software that accepts incoming mail from a mail-transfer system and delivers it to a recipient's mailbox
options.B: An email client used to compose messages
options.C: Software that transfers email between servers
options.D: A server that routes email messages

questions.explanation: A Mail Delivery Agent (MDA) is software that accepts incoming mail from a mail-transfer system and delivers it to a recipient's mailbox.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email provider?

options.A: An organisation or service that provides email accounts, mailboxes and related email infrastructure
options.B: A person who sends emails
options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A software for editing images

questions.explanation: An email provider is an organisation or service that provides email accounts, mailboxes and related email infrastructure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What does the From field indicate in an email?

options.A: The email address or account shown as the sender of the message
options.B: The primary recipient of the message
options.C: The additional recipients who receive a copy
options.D: The subject of the message

questions.explanation: The From field indicates the email address or account shown as the sender of the message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What does the To field indicate in an email?

options.A: The primary recipient or recipients for whom the email is intended
options.B: The sender of the message
options.C: The hidden recipients of the message
options.D: The attachment of the message

questions.explanation: The To field indicates the primary recipient or recipients for whom the email is intended.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What does CC stand for in email?

options.A: Carbon Copy
options.B: Computer Copy
options.C: Confidential Copy
options.D: Central Copy

questions.explanation: CC stands for Carbon Copy in email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the purpose of the CC field in an email?

options.A: To send a visible copy of an email to additional recipients who should be informed but are not necessarily the primary recipients
options.B: To hide the recipients' addresses from each other
options.C: To send the email only to the primary recipient
options.D: To attach files to the email

questions.explanation: The purpose of the CC field is to send a visible copy of an email to additional recipients who should be informed but are not necessarily the primary recipients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What does BCC stand for in email?

options.A: Blind Carbon Copy
options.B: Basic Carbon Copy
options.C: Broadcast Carbon Copy
options.D: Backup Carbon Copy

questions.explanation: BCC stands for Blind Carbon Copy in email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the purpose of the BCC field in an email?

options.A: To send a copy to recipients whose addresses are hidden from other recipients
options.B: To send a visible copy to additional recipients
options.C: To mark the email as important
options.D: To schedule the email for later delivery

questions.explanation: The purpose of the BCC field is to send a copy to recipients whose addresses are hidden from other recipients in the usual message view.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the main difference between CC and BCC?

options.A: CC recipients are generally visible to other recipients; BCC recipients are concealed from other recipients
options.B: CC recipients are hidden; BCC recipients are visible
options.C: CC is used for attachments; BCC is used for the subject
options.D: There is no difference between CC and BCC

questions.explanation: The main difference is that CC recipients are generally visible to other recipients, while BCC recipients are concealed from other recipients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: Can a BCC recipient see the other addresses in the To and CC fields?

options.A: Yes, BCC hides the BCC recipient list, not the visible To and CC fields
options.B: No, BCC hides all addresses in the email
options.C: Only if the sender allows it
options.D: Only if the email has no attachments

questions.explanation: Yes, a BCC recipient can see the other addresses in the To and CC fields. BCC hides the BCC recipient list, not the visible To and CC fields.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: Can recipients normally see the addresses of other BCC recipients?

options.A: No, a recipient generally cannot see the other BCC recipients through the message headers they receive
options.B: Yes, all BCC recipients are visible to everyone
options.C: Only the first BCC recipient is visible
options.D: Only if the email is forwarded

questions.explanation: No, a recipient generally cannot see the other BCC recipients through the message headers they receive.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: When should the To field be used in an email?

options.A: For people who are expected to read, respond to or act on the message
options.B: For people who only need awareness of the message
options.C: For hiding recipients' addresses
options.D: For attaching files

questions.explanation: The To field should be used for people who are expected to read, respond to or act on the message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: When should CC be used in an email?

options.A: For people who need awareness or context but are not the main addressees
options.B: For the primary recipients who must act on the message
options.C: For hiding recipients' addresses
options.D: For sending large attachments

questions.explanation: CC should be used for people who need awareness or context but are not the main addressees.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: When should BCC be used in an email?

options.A: When recipient addresses should be kept private, such as sending a notice to a large group of unrelated recipients
options.B: When all recipients should see each other's addresses
options.C: When the email has no subject
options.D: When sending an email to only one person

questions.explanation: BCC should be used when recipient addresses should be kept private, such as sending a notice to a large group of unrelated recipients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: Should BCC be used to secretly involve someone in a sensitive conversation?

options.A: No, it is generally inappropriate; use transparent communication where practical and follow organisational policy
options.B: Yes, it is always appropriate
options.C: Yes, if the conversation is confidential
options.D: Only if the sender is a manager

questions.explanation: It is generally inappropriate to use BCC to secretly involve someone in a sensitive conversation; use transparent communication where practical and follow organisational policy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: Does Reply All normally include the original BCC recipients?

options.A: No, BCC recipients are not normally exposed or automatically included in Reply All responses
options.B: Yes, all BCC recipients are included
options.C: Only if the sender selects the option
options.D: Only if the email has no CC recipients

questions.explanation: No, BCC recipients are not normally exposed or automatically included in Reply All responses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: Can a BCC recipient's reply reveal that they received the message?

options.A: Yes, if a BCC recipient replies to the sender or others, their participation may become apparent
options.B: No, BCC recipients can never reveal their identity
options.C: Only if they use Reply All
options.D: Only if the email has attachments

questions.explanation: Yes, if a BCC recipient replies to the sender or others, their participation may become apparent.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is Reply in email?

options.A: A command that sends a response to the sender of the selected message
options.B: A command that sends a response to all visible recipients
options.C: A command that forwards the message to another recipient
options.D: A command that deletes the message

questions.explanation: Reply is a command that sends a response to the sender of the selected message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is Reply All in email?

options.A: A command that sends a response to the sender and the other visible recipients of the original message
options.B: A command that sends a response only to the sender
options.C: A command that forwards the message to a new recipient
options.D: A command that archives the message

questions.explanation: Reply All is a command that sends a response to the sender and the other visible recipients of the original message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is Forward in email?

options.A: A command that sends a received message, often including its content and attachments, to another recipient
options.B: A command that sends a response to the sender
options.C: A command that deletes the message
options.D: A command that marks the message as spam

questions.explanation: Forward is a command that sends a received message, often including its content and attachments, to another recipient.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the safest practice when using Reply All?

options.A: Use Reply All only when every included recipient needs the response; otherwise reply only to the relevant person
options.B: Always use Reply All for every email
options.C: Never use Reply All under any circumstances
options.D: Use Reply All only for emails with attachments

questions.explanation: The safest practice is to use Reply All only when every included recipient needs the response; otherwise reply only to the relevant person.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the risk of placing a large public recipient list in the To or CC field?

options.A: It exposes recipients' email addresses to one another and may create privacy or data-protection concerns
options.B: It makes the email send faster
options.C: It reduces the size of attachments
options.D: It automatically encrypts the email

questions.explanation: Placing a large public recipient list in the To or CC field exposes recipients' email addresses to one another and may create privacy or data-protection concerns.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Fields: From, To, CC and BCC
questions.question: What is the difference between a recipient and a sender?

options.A: The sender sends the message; a recipient is an intended person or mailbox that receives it
options.B: The recipient sends the message; the sender receives it
options.C: Both sender and recipient send the message
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: The sender sends the message; a recipient is an intended person or mailbox that receives it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is composing an email?

options.A: Creating a new message by entering recipients, a subject and the message body, and adding any necessary attachments
options.B: Deleting an email from the inbox
options.C: Forwarding an email to another person
options.D: Archiving an email message

questions.explanation: Composing an email is creating a new message by entering recipients, a subject and the message body, and adding any necessary attachments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Send command used for in email?

options.A: It submits the composed message to the email service for transmission
options.B: It saves the message as a draft
options.C: It deletes the message
options.D: It archives the message

questions.explanation: The Send command submits the composed message to the email service for transmission.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Drafts folder in email?

options.A: A folder that stores messages that have been started but not yet sent
options.B: A folder that stores received messages
options.C: A folder that stores deleted messages
options.D: A folder that stores spam messages

questions.explanation: The Drafts folder stores messages that have been started but not yet sent.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Inbox in email?

options.A: The folder or view where incoming email messages are delivered
options.B: The folder that stores sent messages
options.C: The folder that stores draft messages
options.D: The folder that stores deleted messages

questions.explanation: The Inbox is the folder or view where incoming email messages are delivered.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Sent folder in email?

options.A: The folder that stores copies of messages sent from an email account
options.B: The folder that stores received messages
options.C: The folder that stores draft messages
options.D: The folder that stores spam messages

questions.explanation: The Sent folder stores copies of messages sent from an email account, depending on service settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Outbox in email?

options.A: A folder or queue that may hold outgoing messages waiting to be sent
options.B: A folder that stores received messages
options.C: A folder that stores deleted messages
options.D: A folder that stores spam messages

questions.explanation: The Outbox is a folder or queue that may hold outgoing messages waiting to be sent.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Trash or Deleted Items folder in email?

options.A: A folder that temporarily stores messages deleted by the user before permanent removal
options.B: A folder that stores sent messages
options.C: A folder that stores draft messages
options.D: A folder that stores incoming messages

questions.explanation: The Trash or Deleted Items folder temporarily stores messages deleted by the user before permanent removal, subject to the service's retention rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Archive function in email?

options.A: It removes a message from the Inbox view without necessarily deleting it; the message remains available in the account's archive or all-mail view
options.B: It permanently deletes the message from the account
options.C: It moves the message to the Spam folder
options.D: It forwards the message to another recipient

questions.explanation: The Archive function removes a message from the Inbox view without necessarily deleting it; the message remains available in the account's archive or all-mail view.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between deleting and archiving an email?

options.A: Deleting moves a message to Trash or Deleted Items; archiving removes it from the Inbox while retaining it in the account
options.B: Deleting retains the message; archiving permanently removes it
options.C: Both deleting and archiving permanently remove the message
options.D: There is no difference between deleting and archiving

questions.explanation: Deleting moves a message to Trash or Deleted Items; archiving removes it from the Inbox while retaining it in the account.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email attachment?

options.A: A file sent along with an email message, such as a document, image, spreadsheet or PDF
options.B: The subject line of the email
options.C: The signature at the end of the email
options.D: The password of the email account

questions.explanation: An email attachment is a file sent along with an email message, such as a document, image, spreadsheet or PDF.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the paperclip icon commonly indicate in email?

options.A: That a message has an attachment or to open the attachment function
options.B: That the message is important
options.C: That the message is spam
options.D: That the message has been read

questions.explanation: The paperclip icon commonly indicates that a message has an attachment or is used to open the attachment function.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an inline image in email?

options.A: An image displayed within the message body rather than only as a separate downloadable attachment
options.B: An image that is always sent as a separate file
options.C: An image that cannot be viewed in the email
options.D: An image that is automatically deleted

questions.explanation: An inline image is an image displayed within the message body rather than only as a separate downloadable attachment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email draft?

options.A: An unfinished message saved so the sender can edit and send it later
options.B: A message that has already been sent
options.C: A message that has been deleted
options.D: A message that has been marked as spam

questions.explanation: An email draft is an unfinished message saved so the sender can edit and send it later.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a scheduled email?

options.A: An email composed in advance and configured to be sent automatically at a specified future time
options.B: An email that is sent immediately after composing
options.C: An email that is automatically deleted after sending
options.D: An email that is automatically marked as spam

questions.explanation: A scheduled email is an email composed in advance and configured to be sent automatically at a specified future time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email filter or rule?

options.A: A condition-based setting that automatically labels, moves, forwards, deletes or otherwise processes incoming messages
options.B: A tool for editing email attachments
options.C: A password used to access the email account
options.D: A type of email address

questions.explanation: An email filter or rule is a condition-based setting that automatically labels, moves, forwards, deletes or otherwise processes incoming messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email label?

options.A: A tag used by some email services to organise and identify messages; one message may have multiple labels
options.B: A folder that can contain only one message
options.C: A password for the email account
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: An email label is a tag used by some email services to organise and identify messages; unlike a traditional folder, one message may have multiple labels.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email folder?

options.A: A container used to organise messages into categories or groups
options.B: A type of email attachment
options.C: A password for the email account
options.D: A server that stores emails

questions.explanation: An email folder is a container used to organise messages into categories or groups.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email search?

options.A: A feature used to find messages by sender, recipient, subject, date, words or other criteria
options.B: A feature that automatically deletes old emails
options.C: A feature that sends emails automatically
options.D: A feature that encrypts emails

questions.explanation: Email search is a feature used to find messages by sender, recipient, subject, date, words or other criteria.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email read receipt?

options.A: A notification feature that may inform a sender when a recipient has opened a message, if supported and permitted
options.B: A confirmation that the email was delivered to the server
options.C: A receipt for purchasing email storage
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: An email read receipt is a notification feature that may inform a sender when a recipient has opened a message, if supported and permitted by the recipient's service.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email bounce message?

options.A: An automated notification that an email could not be delivered to one or more recipients
options.B: A message that has been forwarded to another recipient
options.C: A message that has been archived
options.D: A message that has been marked as spam

questions.explanation: An email bounce message is an automated notification that an email could not be delivered to one or more recipients.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a soft bounce in email?

options.A: A temporary delivery failure, such as a full mailbox or a temporary server problem
options.B: A permanent delivery failure because the address does not exist
options.C: A message that has been marked as spam
options.D: A message that has been archived

questions.explanation: A soft bounce is a temporary delivery failure, such as a full mailbox or a temporary server problem.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hard bounce in email?

options.A: A permanent delivery failure, often because the recipient address does not exist or is invalid
options.B: A temporary delivery failure due to a full mailbox
options.C: A message that has been forwarded
options.D: A message that has been archived

questions.explanation: A hard bounce is a permanent delivery failure, often because the recipient address does not exist or is invalid.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email quota?

options.A: The storage limit allocated to an email account or mailbox
options.B: The maximum number of emails that can be sent per day
options.C: The maximum size of an email attachment
options.D: The number of recipients allowed in the To field

questions.explanation: An email quota is the storage limit allocated to an email account or mailbox.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What can happen when an email mailbox is full?

options.A: The service may reject or fail to deliver new incoming messages until storage is freed or the quota is increased
options.B: The service automatically deletes all old messages
options.C: The service automatically increases the quota
options.D: The service converts all messages to attachments

questions.explanation: When an email mailbox is full, the service may reject or fail to deliver new incoming messages until storage is freed or the quota is increased.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is SMTP?

options.A: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol; it is used to submit and transfer outgoing email between clients and mail servers or between mail servers
options.B: A protocol used to retrieve email from a server
options.C: A protocol used to synchronise email across devices
options.D: A protocol used to encrypt email messages

questions.explanation: SMTP stands for Simple Mail Transfer Protocol; it is used to submit and transfer outgoing email between clients and mail servers or between mail servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used to send email?

options.A: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
options.B: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3)
options.C: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)
options.D: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)

questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is commonly used to send email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is POP3?

options.A: Post Office Protocol version 3; a protocol used by an email client to retrieve messages from a mail server, commonly by downloading them
options.B: A protocol used to send outgoing email
options.C: A protocol used to synchronise email across multiple devices
options.D: A protocol used to encrypt email messages

questions.explanation: POP3 stands for Post Office Protocol version 3; a protocol used by an email client to retrieve messages from a mail server, commonly by downloading them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocol is commonly associated with downloading email to a client?

options.A: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3)
options.B: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
options.C: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)
options.D: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)

questions.explanation: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is commonly associated with downloading email to a client.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is IMAP?

options.A: Internet Message Access Protocol; it allows an email client to access and manage messages stored on a mail server and synchronise mailbox state
options.B: A protocol used to send outgoing email
options.C: A protocol used to download email to a single device
options.D: A protocol used to encrypt email attachments

questions.explanation: IMAP stands for Internet Message Access Protocol; it allows an email client to access and manage messages stored on a mail server and synchronise mailbox state.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used to synchronise email across multiple devices?

options.A: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)
options.B: POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3)
options.C: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)
options.D: FTP (File Transfer Protocol)

questions.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) is commonly used to synchronise email across multiple devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between POP3 and IMAP?

options.A: POP3 commonly retrieves messages to a client, while IMAP keeps messages on the server and synchronises folders and message state across devices
options.B: POP3 is used for sending email, while IMAP is used for receiving email
options.C: POP3 is more secure than IMAP in all cases
options.D: IMAP downloads emails to a single device, while POP3 keeps them on the server

questions.explanation: The main difference is that POP3 commonly retrieves messages to a client, while IMAP keeps messages on the server and synchronises folders and message state across devices; exact behaviour depends on configuration.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocol is used for outgoing email: SMTP or IMAP?

options.A: SMTP
options.B: IMAP
options.C: Both SMTP and IMAP
options.D: Neither SMTP nor IMAP

questions.explanation: SMTP is used for outgoing email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which protocols are commonly used for incoming email retrieval?

options.A: IMAP and POP3
options.B: SMTP and HTTP
options.C: FTP and SFTP
options.D: TCP and UDP

questions.explanation: IMAP and POP3 are commonly used for incoming email retrieval.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is STARTTLS in email communication?

options.B: A protocol used to send email messages
options.C: A protocol used to download email messages
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: STARTTLS is an SMTP or other protocol extension that upgrades an initially unencrypted connection to a TLS-protected connection when supported.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is commonly used for SMTP submission with implicit TLS?

options.A: Port 465
options.B: Port 587

options.D: Port 995

questions.explanation: Port 465 is commonly used for SMTP message submission with implicit TLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is commonly used for SMTP submission with STARTTLS?

options.A: Port 587
options.B: Port 465

options.D: Port 995

questions.explanation: Port 587 is commonly used for SMTP submission with STARTTLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is commonly used by IMAP with implicit TLS?

options.A: Port 993
options.B: Port 465
options.C: Port 587
options.D: Port 995

questions.explanation: Port 993 is commonly used by IMAP with implicit TLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which port is commonly used by POP3 with implicit TLS?

options.A: Port 995
options.B: Port 465
options.C: Port 587
options.D: Port 993

questions.explanation: Port 995 is commonly used by POP3 with implicit TLS.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is MIME in email?

options.A: Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions; a standard that enables email to carry different content types, character sets and file attachments
options.B: A protocol used to send email messages
options.C: A protocol used to download email messages
options.D: A type of email server

questions.explanation: MIME stands for Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions; a standard that enables email to carry different content types, character sets and file attachments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email header field?

options.A: A named item in the message header, such as From, To, Subject, Date or Message-ID
options.B: The main content of the email
options.C: The attachment included in the email
options.D: The password of the email account

questions.explanation: An email header field is a named item in the message header, such as From, To, Subject, Date or Message-ID.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Message-ID in email?

options.A: A header field containing an identifier intended to uniquely identify an email message
options.B: The password of the email account
options.C: The subject line of the email
options.D: The attachment file name

questions.explanation: Message-ID is a header field containing an identifier intended to uniquely identify an email message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an email client-server connection?

options.A: A connection through which an email application communicates with a mail service to submit, retrieve or manage messages
options.B: A connection between two email attachments
options.C: A connection between two email addresses
options.D: A connection between two email servers only

questions.explanation: An email client-server connection is a connection through which an email application communicates with a mail service to submit, retrieve or manage messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is end-to-end encryption in email?

options.A: A method in which message content is encrypted so that only the intended endpoints hold the keys needed to decrypt it
options.B: A method in which the email provider can read all messages
options.C: A method in which emails are stored unencrypted on the server
options.D: A method in which emails are sent without any security

questions.explanation: End-to-end encryption in email is a method in which message content is encrypted so that, in a properly implemented system, only the intended endpoints hold the keys needed to decrypt it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does ordinary HTTPS webmail automatically mean email is end-to-end encrypted?

options.A: No, HTTPS protects the connection between the browser and the service, but the provider may still be able to access message content unless separate end-to-end encryption is used
options.B: Yes, HTTPS always provides end-to-end encryption
options.C: Yes, but only for emails with attachments
options.D: Yes, but only for emails sent to multiple recipients

questions.explanation: No, ordinary HTTPS webmail does not automatically mean email is end-to-end encrypted. HTTPS protects the connection between the browser and the service, but the provider may still be able to access message content unless separate end-to-end encryption is used.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is SPF in email security?

options.A: Sender Policy Framework; a DNS-based mechanism that helps receiving mail systems check whether a sending server is authorised to send mail for a domain
options.B: A protocol used to send email messages
options.C: A protocol used to download email messages
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: SPF stands for Sender Policy Framework; a DNS-based mechanism that helps receiving mail systems check whether a sending server is authorised to send mail for a domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is DKIM in email security?

options.A: DomainKeys Identified Mail; a mechanism that uses a cryptographic signature in email headers to help verify that a message was authorised by a domain and was not altered in transit
options.B: A protocol used to send email messages
options.C: A protocol used to download email messages
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: DKIM stands for DomainKeys Identified Mail; a mechanism that uses a cryptographic signature in email headers to help verify that a message was authorised by a domain and was not altered in transit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is DMARC in email security?

options.A: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance; a policy and reporting framework that builds on SPF and DKIM to help domain owners manage email authentication and alignment
options.B: A protocol used to send email messages
options.C: A protocol used to download email messages
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: DMARC stands for Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance; a policy and reporting framework that builds on SPF and DKIM to help domain owners manage email authentication and alignment.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Do SPF, DKIM and DMARC guarantee that an email is harmless?

options.A: No, they help authenticate sending domains and reduce certain forms of spoofing, but authenticated messages can still be unwanted or malicious
options.B: Yes, they guarantee that all emails are safe
options.C: Yes, they block all spam messages
options.D: Yes, they encrypt all email content

questions.explanation: No, SPF, DKIM and DMARC do not guarantee that an email is harmless. They help authenticate sending domains and reduce certain forms of spoofing, but authenticated messages can still be unwanted or malicious.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of an email attachment?

options.A: To send a separate file or document along with the message
options.B: To send the email faster
options.C: To encrypt the email message
options.D: To delete the email after sending

questions.explanation: The purpose of an email attachment is to send a separate file or document along with the message.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common file type sent as an email attachment?

options.A: PDF
options.B: EXE
options.C: BAT
options.D: COM

questions.explanation: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, TXT, JPG, PNG, ZIP and other document, image or archive formats are common file types sent as email attachments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the maximum attachment size for every email service?

options.A: There is no universal maximum; limits vary by provider, account type, message encoding and organisational policy
options.B: 25 MB for all email services
options.C: 10 MB for all email services
options.D: 100 MB for all email services

questions.explanation: There is no universal maximum attachment size for every email service; limits vary by provider, account type, message encoding and organisational policy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why can an attachment become larger after being attached to an email?

options.A: Email encoding, such as Base64, adds overhead to binary file data, increasing the transmitted message size
options.B: The attachment is automatically compressed
options.C: The attachment is automatically encrypted
options.D: The attachment is automatically converted to a different format

questions.explanation: An attachment can become larger after being attached to an email because email encoding, such as Base64, adds overhead to binary file data, increasing the transmitted message size.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should be checked before attaching a file to an email?

options.A: Check that it is the correct file, has an appropriate name and format, contains no unintended sensitive information and is within the service's size limit
options.B: Check that the file is larger than the email
options.C: Check that the file is an executable program
options.D: Check that the file has no name

questions.explanation: Before attaching a file, check that it is the correct file, has an appropriate name and format, contains no unintended sensitive information and is within the service's size limit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cloud attachment or cloud link in email?

options.A: A link to a file stored in a cloud service, often shared with specified access permissions instead of attaching the file directly
options.B: An attachment that is stored on the email server
options.C: An attachment that is automatically deleted after sending
options.D: An attachment that is encrypted with a password

questions.explanation: A cloud attachment or cloud link is a link to a file stored in a cloud service, often shared with specified access permissions instead of attaching the file directly.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a file attachment and a cloud-sharing link?

options.A: An attachment is included with the email message; a cloud link points to a file stored remotely, where access depends on sharing permissions and availability
options.B: An attachment is stored remotely; a cloud link is included with the email message
options.C: Both are stored on the email server
options.D: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: The difference is that an attachment is included with the email message; a cloud link points to a file stored remotely, where access depends on sharing permissions and availability.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should cloud-sharing permissions be checked before sending a link?

options.A: The recipient may otherwise be unable to open the file, or the file may be accessible to more people than intended
options.B: The link will not work without permissions
options.C: The file will be automatically deleted
options.D: The email will be marked as spam

questions.explanation: Cloud-sharing permissions should be checked before sending a link because the recipient may otherwise be unable to open the file, or the file may be accessible to more people than intended.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a compressed attachment?

options.A: A file placed inside a compressed archive, such as ZIP, to reduce size or package multiple files together
options.B: A file that has been deleted
options.C: A file that has been encrypted
options.D: A file that has been converted to PDF

questions.explanation: A compressed attachment is a file placed inside a compressed archive, such as ZIP, to reduce size or package multiple files together.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why might an email service block an attachment?

options.A: It may exceed size limits, use a prohibited file type, contain malware indicators or violate organisational security policies

options.C: It may have a descriptive filename
options.D: It may be a PDF file

questions.explanation: An email service might block an attachment because it exceeds size limits, uses a prohibited file type, contains malware indicators or violates organisational security policies.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why are executable attachments risky?

options.A: Executable files can run code and may install malware or perform harmful actions if opened
options.B: Executable files are always too large to send
options.C: Executable files cannot be attached to emails
options.D: Executable files are automatically deleted by email services

questions.explanation: Executable attachments are risky because executable files can run code and may install malware or perform harmful actions if opened.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a recipient do with an unexpected attachment?

options.A: Verify with the sender through a separate trusted channel before opening it, especially if the message is unusual or urgent

options.C: Forward it to all contacts
options.D: Delete the entire email without reading it

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

options.B: The email address of the sender

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should attachment filenames be descriptive?

options.A: A clear filename helps recipients identify the file and reduces confusion or accidental use of the wrong document
options.B: Descriptive filenames make the file smaller
options.C: Descriptive filenames encrypt the file
options.D: Descriptive filenames are required by all email services

questions.explanation: Attachment filenames should be descriptive because a clear filename helps recipients identify the file and reduces confusion or accidental use of the wrong document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.question: What should a sender do if an email is sent to the wrong recipient?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should sensitive information be handled carefully in email?

questions.explanation: Sensitive information should be handled carefully in email because email may be forwarded, misaddressed, stored or accessed by systems and people beyond the intended recipient; use approved secure channels for sensitive data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the best practice before clicking Send on an email?

options.A: Verify recipients, subject, message content, attachments, links, tone and any confidential information
options.B: Send immediately without checking anything

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spam email?

options.C: An email that has been forwarded
options.D: An email that has been archived

questions.explanation: Spam email is unsolicited or unwanted bulk email, often sent for advertising, scams, fraud or malicious purposes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the common name for unsolicited bulk email?

options.A: Spam
options.B: Phishing
options.C: Malware
options.D: Firewall

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a spam email filter?

options.A: A system that identifies and separates suspected unwanted messages from legitimate email
options.B: A system that encrypts all email messages
options.C: A system that forwards all emails to another account
options.D: A system that deletes all incoming emails

questions.explanation: A spam email filter is a system that identifies and separates suspected unwanted messages from legitimate email.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Spam or Junk folder in email?

options.A: A folder where an email service places messages it classifies as suspected spam or unwanted mail
options.B: A folder that stores sent messages
options.C: A folder that stores draft messages
options.D: A folder that stores deleted messages

questions.explanation: The Spam or Junk folder is a folder where an email service places messages it classifies as suspected spam or unwanted mail.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between spam and phishing?

options.A: Spam is unsolicited or unwanted bulk messaging; phishing is a deceptive attempt to steal information or induce harmful action
options.B: Spam is always malicious; phishing is always harmless
options.C: Spam is sent by known senders; phishing is sent by unknown senders
options.D: There is no difference between spam and phishing

questions.explanation: The difference is that spam is unsolicited or unwanted bulk messaging, while phishing is a deceptive attempt to steal information or induce harmful action. A phishing message may also be spam.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mailing list in email?

options.A: A list of email addresses used to distribute messages to subscribers or members
options.B: A list of all emails in the inbox
options.C: A list of email attachments
options.D: A list of email passwords

questions.explanation: A mailing list is a list of email addresses used to distribute messages to subscribers or members.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is every bulk email spam?

options.A: No, legitimate newsletters and notices may be sent in bulk to people who have requested or agreed to receive them
options.B: Yes, all bulk email is spam
options.C: Yes, unless the email has an attachment
options.D: Yes, unless the email is sent during business hours

questions.explanation: No, not every bulk email is spam. Legitimate newsletters and notices may be sent in bulk to people who have requested or agreed to receive them.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a spammer?

options.A: A person or organisation that sends unsolicited bulk messages
options.B: A person who receives spam emails
options.C: A software that filters spam emails
options.D: A type of email attachment

questions.explanation: A spammer is a person or organisation that sends unsolicited bulk messages.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email spoofing?

options.A: The practice of falsifying email sender information, such as the From address, to make a message appear to come from another source
options.B: The practice of sending legitimate bulk email
options.C: The practice of encrypting email messages
options.D: The practice of archiving email messages

questions.explanation: Email spoofing is the practice of falsifying email sender information, such as the From address, to make a message appear to come from another source.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a botnet in relation to spam?

options.C: A type of email attachment
options.D: A software that filters spam emails

questions.explanation: A botnet in relation to spam is a network of compromised devices that can be controlled to send spam or conduct other malicious activities.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a false positive in spam filtering?

options.A: A legitimate email incorrectly classified as spam
options.B: A spam message incorrectly delivered as legitimate mail
options.C: An email that has been encrypted
options.D: An email that has been forwarded

questions.explanation: A false positive in spam filtering is a legitimate email incorrectly classified as spam.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a false negative in spam filtering?

options.A: A spam message that is incorrectly delivered as legitimate mail

options.C: An email that has been encrypted
options.D: An email that has been archived

questions.explanation: A false negative in spam filtering is a spam message that is incorrectly delivered as legitimate mail.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a user do with a suspected spam message?

questions.explanation: A user should mark a suspected spam message as spam or junk using the email service's reporting function and avoid interacting with suspicious links or attachments.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is replying to spam usually unwise?

questions.explanation: Replying to spam is usually unwise because it can confirm that the email address is active and may lead to more unwanted messages or scams.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should users be cautious about clicking Unsubscribe in suspicious emails?

options.A: A deceptive link may lead to a malicious website; use unsubscribe links only in messages from recognisable, legitimate senders
options.B: Unsubscribe links always work instantly
options.C: Unsubscribe links automatically delete the email account
options.D: Unsubscribe links are required by law for all emails

questions.explanation: Users should be cautious about clicking Unsubscribe in suspicious emails because a deceptive link may lead to a malicious website; use unsubscribe links only in messages from recognisable, legitimate senders.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of reporting spam?

options.A: It helps the email provider improve filtering and may support action against abusive senders
options.B: It automatically deletes all emails from the sender
options.C: It encrypts the spam message
options.D: It forwards the spam to all contacts

questions.explanation: The purpose of reporting spam is to help the email provider improve filtering and may support action against abusive senders.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can spam contain malware?

options.A: Yes, spam may include malicious attachments, links or deceptive instructions
options.B: No, spam never contains malware
options.C: Only if the spam has no subject
options.D: Only if the spam is sent during business hours

questions.explanation: Yes, spam can contain malware. Spam may include malicious attachments, links or deceptive instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email flooding?

options.A: Sending a very large volume of messages to overwhelm a mailbox or mail system
options.B: Sending a single email to many recipients
options.C: Encrypting all email messages
options.D: Archiving all email messages

questions.explanation: Email flooding is sending a very large volume of messages to overwhelm a mailbox or mail system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mailing-list unsubscribe?

options.A: A link or mechanism that allows a recipient to stop receiving future messages from a legitimate mailing list
options.B: A link that deletes the email account
options.C: A link that encrypts the email
options.D: A link that forwards the email to all contacts

questions.explanation: A mailing-list unsubscribe is a link or mechanism that allows a recipient to stop receiving future messages from a legitimate mailing list.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is phishing?

options.A: A cyberattack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted person or organisation to trick a victim into revealing information, transferring money, opening malicious files or taking another harmful action
options.B: A method of sending legitimate bulk email
options.C: A method of encrypting email messages
options.D: A method of archiving email messages

questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyberattack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted person or organisation to trick a victim into revealing information, transferring money, opening malicious files or taking another harmful action.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is phishing called phishing?

options.A: The term is a variant of fishing; attackers use deceptive lures to entice victims into revealing valuable information
options.B: It is named after a type of fish
options.C: It is an acronym for 'Personal Information Hacking'
options.D: It is named after the person who invented it

questions.explanation: Phishing is called phishing because the term is a variant of fishing; attackers use deceptive lures to entice victims into revealing valuable information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main objective of phishing?

options.A: To steal credentials, personal or financial information, obtain money, deliver malware or gain unauthorised access
options.B: To send legitimate newsletters
options.C: To encrypt email messages
options.D: To archive email messages

questions.explanation: The main objective of phishing is to steal credentials, personal or financial information, obtain money, deliver malware or gain unauthorised access.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a phishing email?

options.A: A deceptive email that pretends to come from a legitimate source and attempts to manipulate the recipient into taking an unsafe action
options.B: A legitimate email from a known sender
options.C: An email that has been encrypted
options.D: An email that has been archived

questions.explanation: A phishing email is a deceptive email that pretends to come from a legitimate source and attempts to manipulate the recipient into taking an unsafe action.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can a phishing email contain correct personal details?

options.A: Yes, attackers may use publicly available or previously stolen information to make a message appear convincing
options.B: No, phishing emails never contain personal details
options.C: Only if the email has no links
options.D: Only if the email is sent during business hours

questions.explanation: Yes, a phishing email can contain correct personal details. Attackers may use publicly available or previously stolen information to make a message appear convincing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is spear phishing?

options.A: A targeted phishing attack tailored to a specific person, organisation or role
options.B: A phishing attack sent to a large random group
options.C: A phishing attack that only uses SMS
options.D: A phishing attack that only targets children

questions.explanation: Spear phishing is a targeted phishing attack tailored to a specific person, organisation or role.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is whaling in the context of phishing?

options.A: A form of targeted phishing aimed at senior executives or other high-profile individuals
options.B: A phishing attack that uses only whale images
options.C: A phishing attack sent only to children
options.D: A phishing attack that only targets email servers

questions.explanation: Whaling is a form of targeted phishing aimed at senior executives or other high-profile individuals.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is clone phishing?

options.B: A phishing attack that clones the victim's email account
options.C: A phishing attack that only uses phone calls
options.D: A phishing attack that targets only social media accounts

questions.explanation: Clone phishing is an attack in which a legitimate previously received message is copied and altered to include a malicious link or attachment, then resent as if it were an updated version.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Business Email Compromise (BEC)?

options.A: A fraud in which attackers impersonate or compromise a business email account to trick employees or partners into making payments or disclosing information
options.B: A legitimate business email newsletter
options.C: A method of encrypting business emails
options.D: A method of archiving business emails

questions.explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) is a fraud in which attackers impersonate or compromise a business email account to trick employees or partners into making payments or disclosing information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is email spoofing in a phishing attack?

options.A: Falsifying sender information to make a fraudulent message appear to originate from a trusted address or domain
options.B: Sending a legitimate email to many recipients
options.C: Encrypting an email message
options.D: Archiving an email message

questions.explanation: Email spoofing in a phishing attack is falsifying sender information to make a fraudulent message appear to originate from a trusted address or domain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a phishing website?

options.A: A fraudulent website designed to imitate a legitimate site and collect credentials, payment information or other sensitive data
options.B: A legitimate website used for online shopping
options.C: A website that only contains images
options.D: A website that only contains text

questions.explanation: A phishing website is a fraudulent website designed to imitate a legitimate site and collect credentials, payment information or other sensitive data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a malicious link in an email?

options.A: A link that leads to a harmful destination, such as a phishing page, malware download or scam website
options.B: A link that leads to a legitimate website
options.C: A link that automatically deletes the email
options.D: A link that automatically encrypts the email

questions.explanation: A malicious link is a link that leads to a harmful destination, such as a phishing page, malware download or scam website.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should users inspect a link before opening it?

options.B: To make the email send faster

questions.explanation: Users should inspect a link before opening it to check whether the actual destination matches the organisation or purpose claimed in the message; displayed text can differ from the destination URL.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is checking the sender's display name enough to verify an email?

options.A: No, display names can be forged; inspect the full sender address and verify unusual requests through an independent channel
options.B: Yes, the display name is always accurate
options.C: Yes, if the display name is familiar

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a user do after clicking a suspicious link but entering no information?

options.C: Enter personal information to verify the website
options.D: Forward the link to all contacts

questions.explanation: After clicking a suspicious link but entering no information, close the page, do not download or approve anything, and run appropriate security checks; report the incident if required by the organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a user do if they entered a password on a phishing site?

options.D: Share the password with friends

questions.explanation: If a user entered a password on a phishing site, they should, from a trusted device, change the affected password immediately, change reused passwords elsewhere, enable MFA, sign out other sessions where possible and contact the relevant service or organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should a user do if financial details were submitted to a phishing site?

questions.explanation: If financial details were submitted to a phishing site, contact the bank or payment provider immediately through an official channel, request protective action, monitor transactions and report the incident to the appropriate authority.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What should an employee do after receiving a suspected phishing email?

options.D: Delete the email without reporting it

questions.explanation: An employee should not click links or open attachments in a suspected phishing email; report it using the organisation's approved security-reporting process.

questions.question: What is the safest way to verify an unexpected payment request received by email?

options.D: Use the phone number provided in the suspicious email

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Privacy, Security and Responsible Use

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Privacy, Security and Responsible Use
questions.question: Why should recovery information be kept up to date?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Privacy, Security and Responsible Use
questions.question: What is encryption at rest?

options.D: Protection applied to email signatures only

questions.explanation: Encryption at rest is protection applied to stored data, such as messages saved on a mail server or device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Email Privacy, Security and Responsible Use

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
